docs.title: MAMMA MIA Visualization Backend
docs.text: Welcome to the documentation for the MAMMA MIA Visualization Backend.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The MAMMA MIA Visualization Backend is a high-performance FastAPI service designed to serve oceanographic data. Data source comes from MAMMA MIA toolbox which simulates the payload (sensors) and trajectory of a platform (Autonomous Underwater Vehicle). It exposes API endpoints to retrieve:

  • Trajectory data from platforms such as Slocum Glider.
  • Oceanographic sensor readings data from platforms like Autosub Long Range (ALR) and Slocum Glider, including:
    • Sea Water Practical Salinity
    • Sea Water Temperature
    • Mass Concentration of Chlorophyll in Sea Water
  • Multi-dimensional Zarr dataset inspection, metadata and slice query capabilities.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
The backend consists of:

  • FastAPI Application (main.py): Entry point defining app middleware (CORS) and dynamic route inclusion.
  • Zarr Tiler Factory (factory.py): Exposes structured API endpoints for retrieving variables, dimensions, spatial subsets, and data slices.
  • Zarr Reader Core (reader.py): Utilities for interfacing with Zarr stores, reading metadata, performing coordinate projections (pyproj), and slicing data.
  • Utilities (utils/): Helper functions for spatial conversions, timestamp parsing, and array processing.

docs.title: Documentation Structure
docs.text:
• Getting Started with MAMMA MIA backend: Installation, running locally with Uvicorn, and Docker container deployment.
  • API Reference: Detailed information on endpoints, request parameters, response schemas, and interactive Swagger/OpenAPI docs.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: The MAMMA MIA Visualization Backend provides FastAPI endpoints for querying and reading Zarr oceanographic datasets.

docs.title: Interactive API Documentation
docs.text:
When running the application, interactive documentation generated by Swagger UI and ReDoc is available:

  • Swagger UI: http://127.0.0.1:8040/docs
  • ReDoc: http://127.0.0.1:8040/redoc

docs.title: 1. Dataset Variables
docs.text:
Returns a list of data variables available in a specified Zarr dataset URL and group.

  • URL: /zarr_variables
  • Method: GET
  • Query Parameters:
  • url (string, required): Dataset URL or local store path.
  • group (string, optional): Zarr group to inspect.
  • Response: JSON list of variable strings.

docs.title: 2. Dataset Dimensions
docs.text:
Returns dimensions and their shapes for a specified Zarr dataset.

  • URL: /zarr_dimensions
  • Method: GET
  • Query Parameters:
  • url (string, required): Dataset URL or local store path.
  • group (string, optional): Zarr group to inspect.
  • Response: JSON object mapping dimension names to shapes.

docs.title: 3. Time Values
docs.text:
Returns time values for a specified Zarr dataset.

  • URL: /zarr_time_values
  • Method: GET
  • Query Parameters:
  • url (string, required): Dataset URL or local store path.
  • group (string, optional): Zarr group to inspect.
  • Response: JSON list of time value strings.

docs.title: 4. Trajectory Data (CZML)
docs.text:
Returns CZML JSON structure containing datetime, latitude, longitude, and depth for an AUV's trajectory.

  • URL: /zarr_trajectory
  • Method: GET
  • Query Parameters:
  • url (string, required): Dataset URL or local store path.
  • payload_group (string, optional): Zarr group to get AUV's trajectory data.
  • platform_group (string, optional): Zarr group to get AUV's platform data.
  • platform_model_name (string, optional): Attribute to get AUV's platform model name.
  • start_date (string, optional): Start date to filter AUV's trajectory data.
  • end_date (string, optional): End date to filter AUV's trajectory data.
  • Response: JSON CZML object containing position and orientation metrics.

docs.title: 5. Trajectory Data (CSV)
docs.text:
Returns trajectory data (id, latitude, longitude, depth) in CSV format as a file download.

  • URL: /zarr_trajectory_csv
  • Method: GET
  • Query Parameters:
  • url (string, required): Dataset URL or local store path.
  • payload_group (string, optional): Zarr group to get AUV's trajectory data.
  • platform_group (string, optional): Zarr group to get AUV's platform data.
  • platform_model_name (string, optional): Attribute to get AUV's platform model name.
  • start_date (string, optional): Start date to filter AUV's trajectory data.
  • end_date (string, optional): End date to filter AUV's trajectory data.
  • target_depth_format (string, optional): Format to return depth values, either 'Mean Sea Level' or 'WGS84 Ellipsoid'.
  • Response: text/csv file attachment (trajectory.csv).

docs.title: 6. Sensor Metrics
docs.text:
Returns datetime, latitude, longitude, depth, conductivity/salinity, temperature, pressure, and chlorophyll values.

  • URL: /zarr_metrics
  • Method: GET
  • Query Parameters:
  • url (string, required): Dataset URL or local store path.
  • reality_group (string, optional): Zarr group to inspect to get sensor readings.
  • start_date (string, optional): Start date to filter sensor readings.
  • end_date (string, optional): End date to filter sensor readings.
  • Response: JSON object containing time series of sensor metric readings.

docs.title: 7. Metrics Units
docs.text:
Returns measurement units for conductivity, salinity, temperature, pressure, and chlorophyll levels.

  • URL: /zarr_metrics_units
  • Method: GET
  • Query Parameters:
  • url (string, required): Dataset URL or local store path.
  • attributes_group (string, required): Zarr group to inspect to get sensor readings units from attributes.
  • second_sensor (string, required): Sensor name of AUV reading conductivity/salinity, temperature, and pressure values.
  • third_sensor (string, required): Sensor name of AUV reading chlorophyll levels.
  • Response: JSON object mapping metric names to unit strings.

docs.title: 8. Mission Deployments
docs.text:
Returns mission deployments contained within the Zarr dataset.

  • URL: /zarr_mission_deployments
  • Method: GET
  • Query Parameters:
  • url (string, required): Dataset URL or local store path.
  • Response: JSON object detailing mission deployments.

docs.title: CORS Configuration
docs.text: By default, Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) allows requests from http://localhost:8080 (e.g., Angular frontend). Additional origins can be configured in main.py.

docs.title: Getting Started with MAMMA MIA backend
docs.text: This guide will walk you through setting up and running the MAMMA MIA Visualization Backend locally or using Docker.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
MAMMA MIA backend supports Python >=3.10 but Python 3.12 is recommended. Also, it's recommended to use latest version of pip. Alternatively, you can use Docker and Docker Compose for containerised deployments.

fastapi>=0.115.8
zarr>=3.0.2
numpy>=2.2.2
uvicorn>=0.34.0
pandas>=3.0.0
pyproj>=3.7.2
mkdocs>=1.6.0
mkdocs-material>=9.5.0

docs.title: Data
docs.text:
1. Create a folder called data_inputs under assets folder. Donwload data generated from MAMMA MIA toolbox at this link: . Move data to this folder.
  2. To use trajectory data (CSV) endpoint, you need to download a vertical grid file from this link: EGM96 15' global vertical datum grid and move it to PROJ data directory. For an installed PROJ this may be /usr/local/share/proj or /user/share/proj on unix style operating systems. For conda environments this may be /path/to/conda/env/share/proj.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
1. Clone the Repository 

    git clone https://github.com/your-org/mamma-mia-vis-backend.git
cd mamma-mia-vis-backend

  2. Set Up Virtual Environment (Recommended)

    a. Creating a Python virtual environment 

    python3 -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate
    b. Alternatively, create a Conda environment 
    conda create --name mamma-mia-vis-backend
conda activate mamma-mia-vis-backend

  3. Installing Backend Dependencies

    a. Install backend dependencies in the Python environment 

    pip install -r requirements.txt
    b. Alternatively, install backend dependencies from requirements.txt in the Conda environment 
    conda install --file --yes requirements.txt

docs.title: Running Backend API Locally
docs.text:
To start the FastAPI server with auto-reload:

uvicorn main:app --reload --port 8040

Once running, the backend API is available at:

  • Base API URL: http://127.0.0.1:8040
  • Interactive OpenAPI / Swagger Documentation: http://127.0.0.1:8040/docs
  • ReDoc Documentation: http://127.0.0.1:8040/redoc

docs.title: Running Backend API using Docker
docs.text: You can containerise and run the application using Docker or Docker Compose.

docs.title: Using Docker Compose (Recommended)
docs.text:
Docker Compose builds the container image and automatically mounts the local ./assets/ directory for live data access:

docker-compose up

To run in detached (background) mode: 

docker-compose up -d

docs.title: Using Docker Build
docs.text:
If you prefer building and running the container manually:

  1. Build the Image 

    docker build -t mamma-mia-vis-backend .

  2. Run the Container 

    docker run -p 8040:8040 -v $(pwd)/assets:/app/assets mamma-mia-vis-backend

docs.title: Generating & Viewing Documentation
docs.text:
Project documentation is powered by MkDocs with the Material theme.

  • Serve Documentation Locally (with live reload): 

    mkdocs serve
    Open http://127.0.0.1:8000 in your web browser.

  • Build Static HTML Site: 

    mkdocs build
    The compiled site will be generated in the site/ folder.
